key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr coatings, HVAF and HVOF deliver the best overall wear performance, while HVAF provides the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Thermal spray process selection strongly controls coating hardness, wear rate, friction, and corrosion behavior on stainless-steel substrates.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, tribological behavior, and electrochemical corrosion performance.
Ranked coating performance across wear and corrosion to identify process-dependent tradeoffs.
evidence_signal: Hardness increased from APS to HVOF/HVAF (771.4 to about 1162-1166 HV), wear rate dropped sharply versus 304 steel, and HVAF showed the best corrosion metrics (Ecorr -0.37 VSCE, Icorr 1.75 μA/cm², Rp 20438.5 Ω).
watch_item: Performance rankings come from a specific substrate, coating composition, and test condition set, so process optimization may not transfer directly to other alloys or service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
